distinguishing_features: Uses a magnetic-field gradient to act on susceptibility differences between dissolved lithium and impurity species, rather than timed chemical dosing.
Claims continuous, membrane-free lateral separation of dissolved boron and magnesium while retaining lithium.
Adds a membrane and electrokinetic coupling, neither of which is part of the prior art’s dosing-gate mechanism.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Remove dissolved boron and magnesium from lithium brine while retaining lithium, without relying on timed purification-chemical dosing.
parsed.viable_reason: At the stated field gradient, magnetic forces on hydrated ions are far too small to produce meaningful drift during the stated residence time, and the added membrane does not establish selective separation or support the claimed 15% removal.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: A dissolved-ion magnetic-gradient separation mechanism is not a routine parameter change to the closest art’s chemical-dosing procedure, even though the proposed mechanism is physically ineffective as written.
